title: Uthman's copies
hookLine: the caliph Uthman has standard copies sent to the cities

lines: TWO ARMIES, TWO WAYS OF RECITING.
cards: In the time of the caliph Uthman, a commander named Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman came back from a campaign far to the north, in Armenia and Azerbaijan. What alarmed him there wasn't the fighting.

Soldiers from Syria and soldiers from Iraq had been reciting the Qur'an differently from one another, and quarreling about it, each side sure the other was wrong. He went straight to Uthman in Medina.

teach.b: Hudhayfah's plea, as Bukhari records it, was this: rescue this community before they differ over the Book the way earlier peoples differed. Uthman acted.

teach.h: ZAYD AND THREE MEN OF QURAYSH
teach.b: He sent to Hafsah for the sheets gathered under Abu Bakr, and set Zayd ibn Thabit to work again, now with three men of Quraysh.
His instruction: where you differ with Zayd over how to write a word, write it in the dialect of Quraysh, because the Qur'an came down in their tongue.
They made copies, and Uthman sent one to each of the main cities, such as Kufa, Basra and Damascus, and kept one in Medina. Reports differ on how many: four, five, seven.

He returned the sheets to Hafsah and ordered other personal copies burned, so there would be one standard. That was hard for some. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud was unhappy at first about giving up his own copy.
Yet over time the companions accepted Uthman's text, and Ali is reported to have said he would have done the same.
The word for such a copy is mushaf, from sahifah, a sheet: the bound, written Qur'an, the thing on the shelf.
Muslims today say the text in every mushaf follows Uthman's copies, and its spelling is called the Uthmani script.
Tradition links some very old copies, kept today in places like Istanbul and Tashkent, to Uthman's time; researchers debate their dates.

how: Muslims read from a mushaf whose text follows the copies Uthman sent to the cities, and printed copies usually note that they follow the Uthmani script.

games.q: you're Uthman. soldiers from different cities are quarreling over how to recite. what do you do?
o: let each city keep its own copy.
make standard copies and send one to each city.
games.why: Uthman had standard copies made from Hafsah's sheets and sent to the cities: one text, many cities.

practice: Bring an early copy to mind: brown parchment, long slanting letters, carried by camel to a far city, set down in a mosque and read aloud to people who never met the Prophet.
Then let the same words reach you, here, today, and breathe with that distance.
